_comment: SAMPLE question bank for the public portfolio demo. Neutral web-fundamentals content, written for this demo only. The real bank this tool was built for is private study material and is not published. Schema is unchanged: every question carries the passage-grounded explanation it was written from, and 'trap' flags items that test an exception or a commonly-confused pair so review can weight them heavier.

questions.q: A resource has moved permanently to a new URL and you want clients and search engines to update their records. Which status code is correct?
options: 302 Found
301 Moved Permanently
307 Temporary Redirect
410 Gone
questions.explain: 301 is the permanent redirect — caches and crawlers update the stored URL. 302 and 307 are temporary, so the original URL is kept. 410 means the resource is gone with no forwarding address.

questions.q: A request arrives with no credentials at all for a protected endpoint. Which is the correct response?
options: 403 Forbidden
400 Bad Request
401 Unauthorized
404 Not Found
questions.explain: 401 means "you have not authenticated" — the server is asking who you are. 403 means "I know who you are and you still may not have this." The confusable pair is which one implies a known identity: 403 does, 401 does not.

questions.q: Which statement about idempotency is correct?
options: POST is idempotent because the server can deduplicate it
PUT is idempotent — repeating the same request leaves the same end state
Idempotent and safe mean the same thing
Only GET can be idempotent
questions.explain: Idempotent means repeating the request produces the same end state, not that it has no effect. PUT and DELETE qualify; POST does not. Safe is the stricter idea — no state change at all — which is why GET is both safe and idempotent while PUT is only idempotent.

questions.q: What does `Cache-Control: no-store` instruct a client to do?
options: Cache the response but revalidate before every use
Cache the response for zero seconds, then reuse it if the server is down
Never write the response to any cache at all
Cache only in the browser, never in a shared proxy
questions.explain: no-store forbids writing the response anywhere. The one that caches-but-always-revalidates is no-cache — the names read backwards from what they do, which is why they get mixed up. private is the directive that restricts storage to the browser rather than a shared proxy.

questions.q: A browser sends an OPTIONS request before your actual PUT request. What is it doing?
options: Checking whether the server is reachable
A CORS preflight, asking whether the cross-origin request is permitted
Negotiating which HTTP version to use
Requesting the list of methods for documentation
questions.explain: That is a CORS preflight. Non-simple cross-origin requests — anything beyond a basic GET/POST with plain content types — trigger an OPTIONS probe first, and the browser only sends the real request if the response allows the method and headers.

questions.q: Which cookie attribute stops JavaScript on the page from reading a cookie?
options: Secure
SameSite=Strict
HttpOnly
Path=/
questions.explain: HttpOnly hides the cookie from document.cookie, which limits what an XSS payload can steal. Secure only requires HTTPS, and SameSite governs whether the cookie rides along on cross-site requests — a different attack (CSRF), not script access.

questions.q: Body text must meet WCAG 2.1 AA. What is the minimum contrast ratio against its background?
questions.explain: AA requires 4.5:1 for normal body text. 3:1 is the relaxed bar for large text and UI components; 7:1 is the stricter AAA target. The trap is quoting the large-text number for body copy.

questions.q: Why is `outline: none` on a focusable element a problem?
options: It breaks the CSS box model
It removes the visible focus indicator keyboard users rely on to know where they are
It prevents the element from receiving focus at all
It is ignored by every modern browser
questions.explain: The element still takes focus — the user just cannot see it, so anyone navigating by keyboard loses their place. If the default ring clashes with a design, replace it with a visible :focus-visible style rather than removing it.
